Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-02-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: Fireflies.ai auto 
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Daniel Reed (Meadow Head of Security), Aisha Khan (Meadow Cloud Engineer), Tomás Rivera (Meadow Privacy Counsel)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Customer wants region pinning for EU workloads, BYOK/KMS integration, verification of subprocessor list, audit log retention and export. Next steps: send SOC2, produce KMS diagram, schedule pilot.

[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick run through the security questions you flagged — region pinning, KMS, subprocessors, audit logs. Daniel, do you want to kick off with your top concerns?
[00:12] Daniel Reed: Yeah thanks Olivia. Um, main thing is data residency — Meadow has EU customer PII that cannot leave EU processing lanes. We need guarantee that inference for those records never touches US hosts. We heard about Redwood region pinning but need details — how strict is it?
[00:27] Marcus Li: Sure, high level: we have routing policies that can pin traffic by customer or route to specific region endpoints. For Hosted API we support region affinity — requests are served in-region when model and infra are available. If capacity is constrained we can fail closed or fail over depending on policy.
[00:42] Aisha Khan: Be more specific — is that a hard guarantee or best-effort? Our compliance requires no cross-border processing for certain fields.
[00:50] Marcus Li: Right, so by default hosted is region-affine which is best-effort. For enforced guarantees we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/private deployment) or Dedicated with reserved capacity in EU, plus explicit routing rules. Redwood Private gives you a private control plane and the compute in your VPC or our customer-owned region so keys and data never egress.
[01:10] Tomás Rivera: When you say 'private control plane', who manages the control plane and where is it hosted? We need to know if any metadata leaves EU.
[01:18] Priya Nair: Good question. For the VPC on-prem option the control plane is deployed in the customer's AWS account or in their VPC. For the hosted Private option we can offer a control plane hosted in EU-only subnets — but we will enumerate subprocessors. There is also an option to configure audit log export to a customer-owned S3 bucket in their EU account.
[01:35] [02:05] Daniel Reed: Subprocessors — we need the full list and whether any have US access to logs or backups. Also, what about support engineers accessing logs for debugging, do they route through US?
[02:15] Olivia Chen: We maintain a subprocessor inventory; I'll share the canonical spreadsheet. For Private deployments, support requires explicit access requests and we can restrict that to EU-based support ops or operate via jumpbox with zero data exposure. For Hosted accounts some subs may be in US — depends on product. We'll include an export that maps subprocessors to regions.
[02:34] Aisha Khan: KMS — are you able to integrate with our AWS KMS and do customer-managed keys? We can't have Redwood hold plaintext keys.
[02:42] Marcus Li: Yes. We support BYOK: customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM. The typical pattern: encryption at rest uses a data encryption key (DEK) wrapped with the customer's KMS CMK. The unwrapped DEK is only present in the inference runtime memory and stripped after the job. We also support envelope encryption and bring-your-own-KMS for private deployments.
[03:05] Tomás Rivera: What about in-transit? TLS only? Mutual TLS for service-to-service?
[03:09] Marcus Li: All in-transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. For Private we can enable mutual TLS and mTLS between control plane and worker nodes, and between customer VPC endpoints and our service, depending on deployment.
[03:25] [05:00] Aisha Khan: Audit logs — we need event logs for every inference call (metadata at minimum) and a retention of 7 years for certain regulated flows. What kinds of logs do you keep and can we export them?
[05:12] Priya Nair: Our audit trail includes request ID, model version, route, timestamp, originating IP (if in hosted), and any admin actions (deployments, rollouts). We store detailed operational logs and we can ship structured audit logs to a customer S3, Splunk, or SIEM via syslog. Retention in our hosted environment is configurable; for Private you can control retention entirely.
[05:35] Daniel Reed: Are the logs redacted automatically? We can't keep raw PII in long-term logs.
[05:40] Marcus Li: We provide configurable redaction rules — you can set which fields to strip or hash before ingestion. For stronger guarantees, route PII-only inference to Private nodes with no persistent logs, or set up a transient pipeline to redact at ingestion.
[05:55] [07:20] Tomás Rivera: Certification proof — SOC 2 and ISO 27001. I saw a note on your site but we need the actual reports or at least the auditor's attestation letter.
[07:28] Olivia Chen: Absolutely — I'll send SOC 2 Type II report, the summary control matrix, and ISO certificate extract. Note that the full SOC report is under NDA in many cases; we can provide a redacted report or sign an NDA.
[07:45] Daniel Reed: Great. Also want to confirm data residency for backups and metrics — e.g., are backups geo-replicated across regions by default?
[07:55] Priya Nair: In Hosted 기본 — uh, default — some internal backups are geo-replicated for disaster recovery. For customers requiring no cross-border replication we recommend Dedicated or Private with single-region storage. We'll call out which subsystems replicate and provide an options matrix.
[08:20] [10:10] Aisha Khan: Can you explain the routing policy primitives — like if we set 'country: EU-only' at the project level, what happens on a model upgrade or if a new model isn't present in EU?
[10:22] Marcus Li: The routing policy has three modes: strict, best-effort, and fallback-allowed. Strict will reject requests if the required model or capacity isn't available in-region. Best-effort will prefer in-region but may fail over to nearest region. Fallback-allowed will route based on latency/cost policies. For Meadow regulatory flows we'd recommend strict or private deployments.
[10:45] Daniel Reed: Let's say we pick strict and the EU pool is at 95% utilization and latency spikes — will Redwood block calls or queue them?
[10:55] Marcus Li: With strict we block with a 409/503-style response indicating policy violation. With Dedicated you can configure burst capacity and autoscale to avoid that. We can simulate expected load in the pilot.
[11:10] [12:40] Tomás Rivera: Encryption keys lifecycle — how often do you rotate DEKs and CMKs? And what logs exist for key access?
[12:46] Marcus Li: Key rotation is customer-controlled for CMKs in BYOK. For DEKs used inside the runtime we rotate per job or per VM lifecycle; minimal lifetime is minutes. Key access is logged in KMS audit logs (CloudTrail, Stackdriver) and we surface an index of KMS-access events in the audit export.
[13:10] Aisha Khan: If we revoke a CMK, what happens to stored content encrypted under that key? Can Redwood rewrap or is data irrecoverable?
[13:18] Priya Nair: If you revoke a CMK in your KMS, you effectively render wrapped DEKs irrecoverable unless you have a recovery plan. For long-term storage we'd recommend key rotation practices and staged key retirement — we can also support rewrapping with a new key if you export and re-encrypt while you still have access.
[13:36] [15:00] Daniel Reed: Subprocessors again — curious about any monitoring/telemetry vendors that store traces in US. Also curious about DR runbooks and whether they store copies of logs outside EU.
[15:12] Olivia Chen: We'll provide the subprocessor inventory and indicate which vendors have cross-border access. For Private deployments you can opt-out of vendor-managed backups and manage your own snapshot lifecycle. We'll include our DR runbook excerpt for discussion under NDA.
[15:30] [18:00] Aisha Khan: SSO/RBAC — we use Okta SAML for SSO and tight RBAC and SCIM provisioning. What does Redwood support?
[18:12] Marcus Li: We support SAML SSO (Okta, Azure AD) and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based by default with custom roles for read-only, deploy, ops, billing. For audit we keep admin action logs. SCIM events and SSO assertions can be logged to your SIEM if desired.
[18:40] Tomás Rivera: For support access escalation, can we require step-up authentication or approval from our security team?
[18:48] Priya Nair: Yes — for Private we support workflow that routes support access requests through your approval queue and logs the session. For Hosted we can require MFA and limited session tokens and we have just-in-time access tooling.
[19:05] [21:30] Daniel Reed: There's a specific legal nuance: some EU customers want 'no de-identified derivatives' to leave EU. How do you define derivative data for model cache / KV cache?
[21:42] Marcus Li: KV cache and prefix caching can be configured per-route. For sensitive flows we recommend disabling incremental caching or enabling cache encryption and scoping caches to region-only. By derivative we mean any stored representation of request/response used to speed future inference — we can disable or restrict.
[22:00] Aisha Khan: Can we get a sample config to show our auditors?
[22:05] Marcus Li: Yes, we'll provide a sample policy YAML that shows region: EU strict, cache: off, logs: minimal-redacted, kms: external.
[22:20] [25:15] Tomás Rivera: Data subject rights and logs — if a DSAR comes in asking to delete records, do you have a way to remove all references including in logs and caches?
[25:28] Priya Nair: We have a deletion API that can remove records from primary storage and trigger cache invalidation. For logs, if you require PII purging, we can provide log redaction workflows; note that immutable audit trails for compliance may conflict with deletion requests — we can map those case-by-case and propose retention scoping per dataset.
[25:50] Daniel Reed: Okay. Let's talk SLAs briefly — do you provide latency/uptime SLAs for Private or Dedicated?
[26:00] Olivia Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. Private is contractually negotiable and we typically offer uptime and availability SLAs based on the customer's deployment topology.
[26:12] [28:40] Aisha Khan: Regarding telemetry and debugging — are traces or request bodies ever persisted outside runtime memory? Debugging requires some visibility but we want guarantees around PII minimization.
[28:52] Marcus Li: By default we persist telemetry metadata only; payloads are persisted only if you enable request logging. For debugging we have a scrubbing tool and can provide ephemeral access to traces under customer-approved redaction.
[29:10] [31:00] Daniel Reed: Compliance: if we sign up, what's the audit window? We need an annual SOC review and the ability to trigger an audit.
[31:12] Olivia Chen: We can support annual audits; for Private we provide more direct ISO/SOC artifacts and can support auditor access to the environment under NDA. For Hosted we provide standard reports and can provide supplementary evidence pooling.
[31:40] [34:25] Aisha Khan: Network connectivity for the pilot — we want to do an in-region routing smoke test. What ports and IP ranges do you need for a short test?
[34:35] Marcus Li: We'll provide a short spreadsheet with IP ranges and ports (HTTPS 443, optional mTLS endpoints). We'll also propose a small synthetic traffic pattern to validate strict routing under load.
[34:55] [36:10] Tomás Rivera: Can you confirm whether any telemetry or metrics endpoints call home to a US analytics cluster (e.g., for usage metrics)?
[36:20] Olivia Chen: There are analytics subsystems that aggregate at a global plane for product telemetry. For customers with residency requirements we can disable global aggregation and route metrics to EU-only telemetry pipelines; this is typically a Private/Dedicated option. We'll mark that in the artifact we send.
[36:45] [38:00] Aisha Khan: Incident response — if there's a breach, what's your notification window and escalation path?
[38:07] Priya Nair: Our incident response policy: acknowledge within 2 hours of detection, provide initial impact assessment within 24 hours, and a post-incident report within 14 days. For Private deployments we can align on custom SLAs and notify via your security channel.
[38:30] Daniel Reed: Good. One more question: model weight provenance and caching — do any third-party model registries replicate outside EU?
[38:42] Marcus Li: Model artifacts are stored per-deployment; for hosted models we may pull from mirrored registries. For strict residency we recommend hosting your own model artifacts in EU registry and pin the model. We'll include a model artifact checklist.
[39:00] [41:45] Olivia Chen: Quick recap: we will send SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessors sheet with regions, KMS/BYOK diagram, sample policy YAML, IP/port spreadsheet for pilot, and sample DPA language. We'll also set up the pilot week-of 2025-03-03. Does that capture?
[41:58] Daniel Reed: Yes, that helps. Tomás — anything to add on legal?
[42:04] Tomás Rivera: I'll review DPA and provide SCC expectations; we'll coordinate offline with Olivia.
[42:12] Aisha Khan: I'll coordinate the pilot and share a list of datasets and infra details.
[42:20] Marcus Li: One last technical note — when we say 'cache encryption', that's envelope encryption with customer-wrapped DEKs; we'll include pseudocode and a sample API call in the KMS doc.
[42:40] [45:00] Daniel Reed: Thanks all. Any blockers on scheduling the pilot?
[45:06] Olivia Chen: None from our side. We'll send calendar options.
[45:12] Daniel Reed: Great.
[45:20] [47:30] End recording.
